title: A real sequence converges if a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 for all pairs of index maps p, q → ∞ (real-analysis part of supplied Step 6)
statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ. Assume that for all maps p, q : ℕ → ℕ with p(i) → ∞ and q(i) → ∞ as i → ∞ (Tendsto p atTop atTop and Tendsto q atTop atTop), a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 as i → ∞. Then a converges: there is s ∈ ℝ with a(n) → s as n → ∞.
lean_statement: ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ p q : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto p atTop atTop → Tendsto q atTop atTop → Tendsto (fun i => a (q i) - a (p i)) atTop (𝓝 0)) → ∃ s : ℝ, Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 s)
